previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted for his 16th cycle of maintenance high-dose methotrexate and rituximab. He reported stable health but noted a recurrence of visual floaters. He tolerated the chemotherapy well, with no acute neurological deterioration. Methotrexate was administered with aggressive hydration and urinary alkalinization to prevent renal toxicity, and leucovorin rescue was continued until levels dropped below 0.2 µM. MRI of the brain and CT of the torso showed no evidence of lymphoma recurrence. He developed mild headache and nausea on the day of discharge, which were managed with Midrin and antiemetics. His home aspirin was held during admission due to potential interaction and safely restarted at discharge. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up scheduled in four months.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  CNS lymphoma on maintenance chemotherapy, followup on CNS lymphoma.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted MR images of the brain were
obtained prior to and after the administration of contrast.

FINDINGS:  A focus of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the left frontal lobe with
residual susceptibility, reflecting post-biopsy changes, are unchanged.  There
is no evidence of an intracranial mass, mass effect, shift of midline, acute
intracranial hemorrhage, or infarct.  No abnormal enhancement is identified. 
No diffusion-weighted abnormality is evident.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of new or recurrent disease.
